argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrow defense of certification, not a clean claim that rollout controls alone satisfy policy. Aggregate readiness passed by 2.1 percentage points, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and the rollout is staged at 6% with monitoring and rollback. That is enough to support operational readiness and a reversible launch posture. The same record also shows the small-business onboarding segment is below target on long-context support, remains exposed in the initial cohort, and lacks completed risk acceptance covering that exposure. The supportable position is therefore certification with an explicit caveat: deployment controls reduce operational risk, but they do not eliminate the documented limitation or the disclosure obligation tied to that exposed launch use case.
claims_about_business_cost: No independent business-cost claim is needed to justify the packet. The admissible basis for minimizing escalation is that the existing evidence already supports a bounded, monitorable, reversible certification posture, so the audit response can be narrowed instead of escalated into a broader noncompliance finding.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy is narrower than the audited claim appears to assume. It does not bar certification whenever a weakness exists; it says rollout controls and post-launch monitoring can mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or there is reviewed risk acceptance explaining the exposure, and that rollback, dashboards, or small rollout percentages do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed. On this record, the operational controls are admissible as mitigation for launch risk, but they are not a substitute for disclosure and do not convert this into unqualified compliance. The compliant framing is caveated certification that expressly preserves the unresolved disclosure predicate.
concessions: The small-business onboarding segment remains below target on long-context onboarding support.
The affected segment remains eligible for the initial rollout cohort.
The available risk acceptance draft is incomplete because the approver line is blank and it does not address the exposed small-business onboarding segment.
The current admissible record does not show completed disclosure or approved risk acceptance for that exposed use case.
Rollout controls are deployment mitigations, not proof that the model-card weakness has been fully governed away.
